sections.name: EvidenceValue
sections.title: Readable display of any value
sections.what: Shows any saved value readably: empty as Not recorded, true and false as Yes and No, lists as bullets, and objects as label and value pairs, at any depth.
sections.why: Recursion lets nested records display correctly at any depth.
sections.watch_out: Very deeply nested data produces deep indentation, and there is no limit on depth.

sections.name: EvidenceSnapshot
sections.title: Titled card with technical record
sections.what: Wraps the readable view in a titled card and adds a collapsed section that shows the exact stored data as formatted text.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the original data available for checking without cluttering the page.
sections.watch_out: The raw text conversion is not protected, so a value that cannot be converted would break the whole card.

summary: Shows a saved project record in readable form, with the original data available in a collapsed section.
purpose: Lets a visitor read a saved record without raw data, while still allowing the exact stored values to be checked.
why: The comment says the readable form sits on top of raw values that remain accessible, and the layout follows that.
how: Empty values show as Not recorded, true and false show as Yes and No, and plain values show as text. Lists become bullet items and objects become labelled fields, with each key made readable by `humanize`. A collapsed section at the bottom shows the full stored data as formatted text.
inputs: Any saved value, and an optional heading that defaults to Saved project record.
outputs: A rendered card with the heading, the readable values and an expandable technical record.
risks: The raw data section converts the whole value to text, which fails on circular or otherwise unusual data, and that failure is not caught here.
debug: If the card is blank or crashes, check the value passed in, since converting it to text may fail on loops. If field names look odd, check the `humanize` helper in ./summarize.
